arxiv-1903-10334.title: An Upper Bound on the Number of Discrete States Possible for the Human Brain
arxiv-1903-10334.creator: Jon Borresen 1 , Killian O’Brien
arxiv-1903-10334.description: Abstract Human brains are arguably the most complex entities known. Composed of billions of neurons, connected via a highly detailed structure where the underlying method by which functionality occurs is still debated. Here we consider one theory for neural coding, synchronization coding, which gives rise to the highest possible number of discrete states that a brain could exist in.

arxiv-2102-03248.title: Quantum computing hardware in the cloud: Should a computational chemist care?
arxiv-2102-03248.creator: Alessandro Rossi, Paul G. Baity, Vera M. Schäfer, Martin Weides
arxiv-2102-03248.description: Abstract Within the last decade much progress has been made in the experimental realisation of quantum computing hardware based on a variety of physical systems. Rapid progress has been fuelled by the conviction that sufficiently powerful quantum machines will herald enormous computational advantages in many fields, including chemical research.

arxiv-2105-12946.title: Uncertainty-aware Self-supervised Target-mass Grasping of Granular Foods
arxiv-2105-12946.creator: Kuniyuki Takahashi, Wilson Ko, Avinash Ummadisingu, Shin-ichi Maeda
arxiv-2105-12946.description: Abstract Food packing industry workers typically pick a target amount of food by hand from a food tray and place them in containers. Since menus are diverse and change frequently, robots must adapt and learn to handle new foods in a short time-span.

arxiv-2211-01708.title: Ionising feedback from an O star formed in a shock-compressed layer 2019 Ionising feedback from an O star formed in a shock-compressed layer – References
arxiv-2211-01708.creator: A. P. Whitworth, F. D. Priestley, S. T. Geen
arxiv-2211-01708.description: Abstract We develop a simple analytic model for what happens when an O star (or compact cluster of OB stars) forms in a shock compressed layer and carves out an approximately circular hole in the layer, at the waist of a bipolar H ii Region (H ii R).

arxiv-2312-17374.title: Effective Equilibrium Theory of Quantum Light-Matter Interaction in Cavities: Extended Systems and the Long Wavelength Approximation
arxiv-2312-17374.creator: Mark Kamper Svendsen, Michael Ruggenthaler, Hannes Hübener, Christian Schäfer, Martin Eckstein, Angel Rubio, Simone Latini
arxiv-2312-17374.description: Abstract When light and matter interact strongly, the resulting hybrid system inherits properties from both constituents, allowing one to modify material behavior by engineering the surrounding electromagnetic environment. This concept underlies the emerging paradigm of cavity materials engineering, which aims at the control of material properties via tailored vacuum fluctuations of dark photonic environments.

arxiv-2409-08092.title: Modeling Snow on Sea Ice using Physics Guided Machine Learning
arxiv-2409-08092.creator: Ayush Prasad, Ioanna Merkouriadi, Aleksi Nummelin
arxiv-2409-08092.description: Abstract Snow is a crucial element of the sea ice system, affecting the sea ice growth and decay due to its low thermal conductivity and high albedo. Despite its importance, present-day climate models have a very idealized representation of snow, often including just 1-layer thermodynamics, omitting several processes that shape its properties.

britannica-1911-transcendentalism.title: Transcendentalism (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-transcendentalism.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-transcendentalism.description: Article 'Transcendentalism' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 27), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. In general use the term is applied rather promiscuously and frequently by way of criticism to an attitude of mind which is imaginative, aloof from mundane affairs and unmoved by practical considerations. The most famous example of the pseudo-philosophic use of the term is for a movement of thought which was prominent in the New England states from about 1830 to 1850.

pmc-10692085.title: Digitally-enhanced dog behavioral testing
pmc-10692085.creator: Nareed Farhat, Teddy Lazebnik, Joke Monteny, Christel Palmyre Henri Moons, Eline Wydooghe, Dirk van der Linden, Anna Zamansky
pmc-10692085.description: Behavioral traits in dogs are assessed for a wide range of purposes such as determining selection for breeding, chance of being adopted or prediction of working aptitude. Most methods for assessing behavioral traits are questionnaire or observation-based, requiring significant amounts of time, effort and expertise.

pmc-11700273.title: Prevalence of polycystic ovary syndrome among infertile women in the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries: A systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-11700273.creator: Zufishan Alam, Saleh Alseari, Mahra Alameemi, Mayytha Alzaabi, Reem Alkhoori, Linda Östlundh, Omar Melhem, Mohammed Altigani Abdalla, Rami H. Al-Rifai
pmc-11700273.description: BackgroundPolycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is a significant contributor to female infertility and other various metabolic disorders. This systematic review estimates the prevalence of PCOS among infertile women in the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries.MethodsThe study searched five databases (PubMed, Embase, CINAHL, Web of Science, and SCOPUS), from their inception to 2022 for observational studies conducted in GCC countries.

pmc-12561817.title: Making Sense of Action Bias in Higher Education: Pedagogical Insights on Critical Thinking
pmc-12561817.creator: Faith Jeremiah, Robert Istvan Radics
pmc-12561817.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Action bias, the cognitive tendency to favor action over inaction regardless of its necessity, has been extensively studied across domains such as behavioral economics, organizational behavior, and policy development. However, its manifestation in educational contexts remains critically underexplored. In the digital age, with an abundance of both factual and misleading information, the persistence of action bias within education jeopardizes the cultivation of initial critical thinking capable of addressing multifaceted global challenges.

pmc-12629485.title: Using machine learning for detection of Parkinson’s disease and mild cognitive impairment
pmc-12629485.creator: Anthaea-Grace Patricia Dennis, Sarah L. Martin, Robert Chen, Philip Gerretsen, Antonio P. Strafella, Gyan Prakash Modi, Gyan Prakash Modi, Gyan Prakash Modi
pmc-12629485.description: BackgroundParkinson’s disease is a movement disorder featuring motor symptoms and cognitive decline, which can manifest as mild cognitive impairment. The incidence of mild cognitive impairment increases with disease progression, and Parkinson’s disease can cause significant disability, therefore, identification of Parkinson’s disease and mild cognitive impairment in Parkinson’s disease is imperative.

pmc-12739191.title: The Determinants of Against Medical Advice Hospital Discharges
pmc-12739191.creator: Aditya Kaliath, Jamie L Romeiser, Aaron Shaykevich, Ivayla I Geneva
pmc-12739191.description: Background: Discharges against medical advice (AMA) are associated with adverse patient outcomes, higher readmission rates, and increased hospital expenses. Understanding the determinant of AMA is expected to guide the development of preventive measures.Methods: A retrospective cohort study comparing adult inpatient AMA and non-AMA discharges at SUNY Upstate Medical University Hospital over a one-year period.

pmc-13396081.title: Differential Effects of High and Low Frequency Subthalamic Nucleus Deep Brain Stimulation on Force Steadiness in Patients with Parkinson’s Disease: An Exploratory Study
pmc-13396081.creator: Amin Olamazadeh, Steffen Brenner, Daniela Souza de Oliveira, Martin Regensburger, Alessandro Del Vecchio, Thomas M Kinfe
pmc-13396081.description: IntroductionDeep brain stimulation of the subthalamic nucleus (STN-DBS) is an established therapy for patients with Parkinson’s disease (PD). However, the frequency-dependent impact on force steadiness remains largely unknown. This explorative study investigated how stimulation frequency and disease severity influence force steadiness during precision pinch.

pmc-13516076.title: In Vitro and In Vivo Antiviral Activity of a Modified Medium-Chain Fatty Acid Against Porcine Reproductive and Respiratory Syndrome Virus
pmc-13516076.creator: Nader Maher Sobhy, Valeria Lugo-Mesa, Christiana Rezk Bottros Youssef, Cecilia Balestreri, Yuan-Tai Hung, Gary D. Reznik, Declan C. Schroeder, Sagar Mal Goyal
pmc-13516076.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Porcine reproductive and respiratory syndrome virus (PRRSV) causes significant economic losses in the global swine industry, partly because current vaccination strategies offer limited protection against heterologous viral strains. Since modified medium-chain fatty acids (mMCFA) offer enhanced structural stability and antimicrobial properties compared with unmodified MCFA, we evaluated a proprietary mMCFA blend (D-Strike, Devenish Nutrition) against PRRSV in vitro and in vivo. In vitro efficacy was assessed using TCID50 assays on MARC-145 cells and a viability qPCR (V-qPCR).

pmc-13593251.title: Median nerve in the distal forearm: A Cadaveric Morphometric Study
pmc-13593251.creator: Ceren Uğuz Gençer, Hüseyin Aydoğmuş, Mustafa Deniz Yörük, Zeynep Nisa Karakoyun, Mehmet İlkay Koşar, Hasan Tetiker
pmc-13593251.description: The median nerve (MN) is a main peripheral nerve that includes superficial motor and sensory fibers in the distal forearm. The proximity of the MN to the forearm muscle tendons and neurovascular structures enhances its clinical significance. The safety of invasive procedures in this area relies on a thorough understanding of the nerve morphometric characteristics.

pmc-13614808.title: Double Threat in a Newborn: High Anorectal Malformation with Pouch Colon and Bilateral Multicystic Dysplastic Kidneys – A Rare Case Report
pmc-13614808.creator: Shweta Patil, Amit Kumar Sinha, Shreyas Dudhani, Nahil Najeeb
pmc-13614808.description: The coexistence of bilateral multicystic dysplastic kidneys (MCDKs) and high anorectal malformation with pouch colon is exceptionally rare. The combination results in a nonsurvivable condition due to complete renal failure, posing complex diagnostic and management challenges. A full-term male neonate presented with absent anal opening, limb and auricular deformities, and progressive anuria since birth. Antenatal history was unavailable.
